//: Vercel hosts the dashboard. It cannot host the rest of this app: the API
holds a Socket.io server and a Postgres LISTEN connection open, and n8n
and Ollama are long-running servers of their own. All of that needs a
real host; docker-compose.prod.yml is built for one.
So these rewrites point /api, /uploads and /socket.io at that host, which
keeps the dashboard and the API on ONE origin as far as the browser is
concerned. That matters twice: the session cookie is SameSite=Lax and
would not be sent cross-site, and OAUTH_REDIRECT_BASE has to be the
dashboard's own origin or every marketplace callback arrives signed out.
TO FINISH THIS: replace backend.invalid below with your API host, set
PUBLIC_URL and OAUTH_REDIRECT_BASE on the backend to this Vercel URL, and
redeploy. `.invalid` is reserved and can never resolve, so until then the
dashboard fails fast and says so rather than hanging or reaching a
stranger's server.
One caveat that does not go away: Vercel's rewrites do not carry a
WebSocket upgrade, so the realtime queue falls back to HTTP polling. It
works, it is just not a socket. Serving the dashboard from the same host
as the API (the nginx in docker-compose.prod.yml already does) avoids it.
The last rewrite is the single-page fallback and has to stay last. Vercel
checks the filesystem before it applies rewrites, so index.html, assets/,
sw.js, manifest.webmanifest and the icons are served as themselves and
only a path with no file behind it reaches it. Listing those exceptions
by hand would be one more place to forget an icon.
